articles.title: Bayou Hex Burlap
articles.summary: Tiny moss-dark burlap hex weave with stitched bone knots; near-invisible coverage, faint matte grit. Reads as a plain slightly fabric-textured sheen; the weave is gone and only a faint dryness remains.
articles.what: Reference-backed voodoo overlay - moss-dark burlap hex weave, stitched bone knots, root bindings, and swamp grit remapped into dynamic M/R/CC spec response Up close: A very fine cloth-like checker of woven threads, 8-10 px, showing as a faint plaid of tiny horizontal and vertical light dashes inside the highlight. No hex shapes are readable at this scale; it feels like coarse linen weave. From a distance: Reads as a plain slightly fabric-textured sheen; the weave is gone and only a faint dryness remains. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Voodoo Inspired (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: trim, under stripes, numbers.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Voodoo Inspired", or search for "Bayou Hex Burlap".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic base
Sides under graphics for a woven background
Numbers unaffected; weave too fine to matter.
Nearly nothing: a faint linen speckle in the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not a green swamp or moss colour: it adds no colour, only weave in the shine
Not carbon fibre: the weave is plain over-under linen, not diagonal twill
Avoid: gloss bases that hide the weave, large body panels needing visible texture.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
